SELECT 
  fish_date_doy AS doy,
  cls,
  COUNT(*) as boats,
  SUM(yt) as total_yt,
  ROUND(SUM(yt)::FLOAT / NULLIF(SUM(anglers), 0), 3) as avg_yt_per_angler
FROM trips 
WHERE fish_date_season = 2
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, cls

# Analyze S2 seasonal pattern: peaks and class performance
trips_s2 = tables['trips'][tables['trips']['fish_date_season'] == 2].copy()

# Group by fishing date and class to see daily patterns
daily_class = trips_s2.groupby(['fish_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'boat': 'count'
}).reset_index()

# Compute yt_per_angler
daily_class['yt_per_angler'] = daily_class['yt'] / daily_class['anglers'].replace(0, 1)

# Filter to key DOY ranges
spring_peak = daily_class[(daily_class['fish_date_doy'] >= 140) & (daily_class['fish_date_doy'] <= 175)]
fall_peak = daily_class[(daily_class['fish_date_doy'] >= 260) & (daily_class['fish_date_doy'] <= 305)]

# Find top signals
top_spring = spring_peak.nlargest(10, 'yt_per_angler')[['fish_date_doy', 'cls', 'yt', 'anglers', 'yt_per_angler']]
top_fall = fall_peak.nlargest(15, 'yt_per_angler')[['fish_date_doy', 'cls', 'yt', 'anglers', 'yt_per_angler']]

print("=== SPRING PEAK (DOY 140-175) - TOP SIGNALS ===")
print(top_spring.to_string())

print("\n=== FALL PEAK (DOY 260-305) - TOP SIGNALS ===")
print(top_fall.to_string())

# Class breakdown for fall peak to understand multi-day dominance
print("\n=== FALL PEAK BY CLASS ===")
fall_by_class = fall_peak.groupby('cls').agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'boat': 'count'
}).reset_index()
fall_by_class['yt_per_angler'] = fall_by_class['yt'] / fall_by_class['anglers'].replace(0, 1)
fall_by_class = fall_by_class.sort_values('yt', ascending=False)
print(fall_by_class.to_string())
